chunks: And the Sheikh, may God have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili,
who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) speaking regarding taqsir (shortening of prayer) in salat.
He said: A barid within a barid [equals] twenty-four miles.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: taqsir — the obligatory shortening of four-rak'ah prayers to two rak'ahs for a qualifying traveler (qasr prayer)
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: barid — classical unit of distance equal to 4 farsakhs (~22 km); 'barid fi barid' = 8 farsakhs = minimum travel distance for qasr

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance (masafat al-qasr) that obliges a traveler to shorten their prayer (taqsir) according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the minimum travel distance (masafah) that obliges a traveler to perform taqsir — shortening four-rak'ah prayers to two. The Imam defines this threshold as 'a barid within a barid' (barid fi barid), which equals twenty-four miles (eight farsakhs), a formulation that became the standard criterion in Imami fiqh for the obligation of qasr prayer during travel.
